sub_scenario.one_line: mining operations auditor: itinerary A first for the buffer days

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the audit workpapers and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The site itinerary review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Long charter flights themselves are painless; I sleep on planes better than in hotels.
The travel is not the cost.
Never has been.
Someone new shadowed me in the field office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the inspection sequences into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.

My clean-audit streak runs through itineraries with a buffer day after the charter; both fully clean site audits this year had that day, and my workpaper timestamps show the difference in checking depth.
The buffer day shows up in the workpapers themselves.
In the timestamps, plainly.
Same-day short hops between nearby sites are fine.
Short transitions carry no penalty.
None I have ever logged.
I archived last cycle's notes on the site itinerary and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The audit committee praised exactly those two audits by name at the mid-year review.
The buffered work is the recognized work.
Recognized by name.
A vendor call about the audit workpapers ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the field office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the inspection sequences.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the site itinerary records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
Two itineraries are offered for the spring rotation: itinerary A includes the arrival buffer day at each site, itinerary B lands and begins auditing the same afternoon.
One itinerary carries your streak's condition; one deletes it.
Deletes it at every single site.
I sketched next week's plan for the inspection sequences before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the audit workpapers updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
Both itineraries cover identical site lists and count identically for the rotation.
The formal coverage cancels out.
Entirely out.
The regional manager calls same-day starts a sign of audit teams that respect site time.
Site-time respect framing.
Framing that never read my workpapers.
I closed the week by updating the field office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Rotation preferences close Monday: itinerary A with buffer days or same-day itinerary B first?
